items.stem:
Triangle P has vertices (2, 2), (5, 2) and (2, 3).
The point (1, 1) and the line y = 1 are shown on the grid.

parts.t:
Triangle P is rotated through 90° clockwise about the point (1, 1) to give triangle Q.
Find the coordinates of the vertices of triangle Q.

Triangle Q is reflected in the line y = 1 to give triangle R.
Write down the coordinates of the vertices of triangle R.
Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle P directly onto triangle R.

sols: Measure each vertex from the centre (1, 1); a 90° clockwise turn sends ‘a right, b up’ to ‘b right, a down’.
(x, y) → (y, −x) relative to the centre
(2, 2): 1 right, 1 up → 1 right, 1 down → (2, 0)
(5, 2): 4 right, 1 up → 1 right, 4 down → (2, −3)
(2, 3): 1 right, 2 up → 2 right, 1 down → (3, 0)
Vertices of Q: (2, 0), (2, −3) and (3, 0)
Reflection in y = 1: (x, y) → (x, 2 − y).
Vertices of R: (2, 2), (2, 5) and (3, 2)
Compare P with R: (2, 2) → (2, 2), (5, 2) → (2, 5), (2, 3) → (3, 2). The coordinates have simply been swapped.
a rotation followed by a reflection is always a reflection
Reflection in the line y = x
check: (2, 2) lies on y = x and is invariant ✓
